blueprint_topic: Management of Care — objective documentation, functional evidence, professional role boundaries, and Social Security disability adjudication
stem: A client with a persistent orthopedic impairment asks the nurse to write in the chart that the client is "legally disabled" so Social Security will approve benefits. Which response by the nurse is most appropriate?

options.A: Document objective assessment findings and observed functional limitations, and explain that SSA determines disability using the complete evidence.
options.B: Record that the client is legally disabled when mobility limitations are present, because the treating nurse's conclusion can establish benefit eligibility.
options.C: Document the orthopedic diagnosis and reported symptoms but omit functional observations because SSA determines work capacity from the diagnosis itself.
options.D: Refer the client to the prescribing provider and leave nursing functional findings out of the record because they are not relevant to disability review.

rationale: A is correct. Current Social Security Administration guidance states that health professionals provide medical evidence about the nature and severity of impairments and information about what the claimant can still do despite those impairments. SSA explicitly states that a medical source is neither asked nor expected to decide whether a claimant is disabled. SSA considers medical and nonmedical evidence and evaluates how impairments affect work-related function, including sitting, standing, walking, lifting, carrying, pushing, pulling, postural activities, concentration, and other work demands. The nurse should therefore document accurate objective findings and observed functional limitations within nursing scope rather than enter a legal eligibility conclusion. B is incorrect because a treating nurse's chart statement does not itself establish Social Security disability eligibility. C is incorrect because SSA evaluates functional capacity and work-related limitations, not merely the diagnosis label. D is incorrect because appropriate nursing observations and functional findings remain clinically relevant evidence; referral to another clinician does not justify omitting accurate nursing documentation.
educational_objective: Document objective clinical and functional findings relevant to disability evaluation while maintaining the boundary between clinical evidence and SSA's legal disability determination.
source_organization: U.S. Social Security Administration (SSA); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Role of the Medical and Education Professional; Part II - Evidentiary Requirements; How We Decide If You Are Disabled (Step 4 and Step 5); 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: Current SSA disability-evaluation pages rechecked 2026-08-20; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: SSA 'Role of the Medical and Education Professional' lines 63-80: health professionals may provide medical evidence; the claimant's medical source supplies evidence on impairment nature/severity; the medical source is neither asked nor expected to decide whether the claimant is disabled and is instead asked about work-related physical or mental abilities. SSA 'Part II - Evidentiary Requirements' lines 68-85: medical evidence is central; SSA considers all medical/nonmedical evidence to assess effect on work function and requires evidence about whether work-related physical/mental activities can still be performed. Lines 98-108: reports include pertinent objective findings and what the claimant can still do, including sitting, standing, walking, lifting, carrying, pushing/pulling, reaching and postural activities. SSA 'How We Decide If You Are Disabled' lines 100-124: SSA uses its disability process and assesses RFC from all evidence, including physical, postural, sensory, cognitive and social work-related abilities. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Management of Care: accurate documentation, legal/ethical requirements, advocacy, interdisciplinary communication, and professional role boundaries.
source_claim_supported: Current SSA sources directly support the distinction between clinical/functional evidence and the legal disability determination, and directly support work-related functional documentation as relevant evidence. NCSBN supports accurate documentation and professional/legal role boundaries.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: document client information accurately, follow legal and ethical requirements, advocate for client needs, communicate with interdisciplinary systems, and remain within professional role boundaries.
pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan evidence was visually verified earlier in this cleanup session. SSA evidence used for Q1876 is current HTML; no new PDF evidence is used.
correction_summary: Original Q1876 had a 243-character correct answer, much shorter distractors, and absolute-word cues. The item was rebuilt with closely balanced action-oriented options and without absolute distractor language. The key now tests the correct boundary: document objective nursing findings and functional limitations, but do not convert the chart into a legal Social Security disability determination.

option_audit.A: Correct; matches SSA's evidence model and preserves the nurse's role in accurate clinical/functional documentation without making the legal determination.
option_audit.B: Plausible advocacy overreach; incorrect because a nurse's conclusion that a client is legally disabled does not establish SSA eligibility.
option_audit.C: Plausible diagnosis-focused misconception; incorrect because SSA explicitly evaluates work-related functional capacity, not diagnosis name alone.
option_audit.D: Plausible role-boundary overcorrection; incorrect because accurate nursing functional observations remain relevant and should not be intentionally omitted.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on only/all/always/never/must-type absolute wording.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 147, B 156, C 152, D 152 characters; the correct answer is not the longest and choices are tightly balanced.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are documentation/communication responses to the same request and require role/evidence reasoning.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified in the pre-stage audit. B makes an adjudicative conclusion, C omits central functional evidence, and D wrongly excludes relevant nursing findings. Post-fetch adversarial reread remains required.
